Subject: POC Capacity & Success Criteria — Horizon trial plan

Hi Marcus / Olivia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and a proposed POC plan so we can lock timelines and ownership. High-level notes from our call: 

- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for real-time summarization feature in Horizon’s customer portal. Primary success criteria listed below.
- Sample traffic: ~250 TPS peak (bursty), ~10M tokens/day expected during active test days. Typical request length ~800 tokens (avg).
- Latency target: 95th percentile < 350ms for single-request inference (no heavy reranking).

Proposed POC capacity profile (please confirm):
- Reserved baseline: 2 x A100 (40GB) GPUs dedicated to Horizon for stable runs.
- Autoscale pool: up to 6 x A100 for burst windows (policy-based, warm-up 5–10 minutes).
- Expected concurrency per GPU: 8–12 simultaneous streams depending on batching.

Evaluation plan & success criteria (draft):
1) Functional: Generated summaries match your quality thresholds (ROUGE / human pass rate >= 85%).
2) Performance: 95p latency < 350ms under target load; throughput scales to expected TPS with <10% error rate.
3) Reliability: No more than one transient failure per 24h test window; graceful fallback to smaller model under load.
4) Cost telemetry review: tokenized cost within agreed budget window.

Ownership and roles:
- Marissa Cole (me): commercial lead, exec touchpoint, schedule/stakeholder coordination.
- Dev Patel: technical lead — infra config, load tests, and capacity tuning.
- Evelyn Hart: customer success — onboarding and trial acceptance criteria.

Suggested timeline:
- Week of Mar 9: kickoff + networking + onboarding (VPN/keys, sample data flow).
- Week of Mar 16: integration + smoke tests; initial load tests mid-week.
- Week of Mar 23: ramped load tests, final evaluation, decision by Fri 3/27.

Attachments: we will share a capacity estimate workbook and our onboarding checklist after this email.

Please confirm: (A) reserved baseline as above or prefer fewer reserved GPUs + larger burst? (B) any internal compliance/whitelisting needed ahead of Mar 9?

If that works I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff with Dev and Evelyn next Tuesday.

Best,
Marissa Cole

marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Hi all —

Thanks Marissa — added some operational detail below so we have a concrete starting point for the kickoff. I attached a short workbook (poc_capacity_estimate.xlsx) with the assumptions and cost ballpark. Key points: 

1) Baseline configuration and expected throughput
- 2 x A100 (40GB) as reserved nodes: target baseline concurrency = 16–20 streams (8–10 per GPU) with moderate batching (batch size 4–8).
- Warm cache expected to reduce per-token execution ~15–20% after first 30–50 requests.
- Autoscale to 6 x A100 for sustained bursts; autoscale policy: trigger at 70% GPU util for 30s, scale step +1 node with cooldown 90s.

2) Load-test plan (scripted):
- Phase 0: smoke — connectivity, model load, KV cache validation (Day 0).
- Phase 1: ramp — linear ramp to 50% target TPS over 30m, measure p50/p95/p99.
- Phase 2: spike tests — 2x target TPS sustained for 5m windows, observe queueing and tail latency.
- Phase 3: endurance — 4h run at expected daily peak distribution.

3) Metrics we’ll capture (for each run):
- Latency percentiles (p50,p95,p99), error rate, GPU util, queue lengths, tokens/sec, avg batch size.
- Quality sampling: 200 random requests per test run sent to Horizon’s human-review tool for pass/fail labeling.

4) Network & infra notes:
- We’ll need CIDR whitelisting for Redwood egress IPs (I’ll send ranges in separate email).
- If Horizon wants to route through a private VPC peering, provide VPC IDs and contact.

Open/assumptions: model size and KV cache footprint — if you’re running a larger context (>4k tokens) we should evaluate memory pressure; may recommend 3 x A100 baseline instead. Workbook shows both 2x and 3x baseline scenarios.

Next steps from my side: finalize load-test scripts and provide a short runbook for your infra team before kickoff.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai

Attachment: poc_capacity_estimate.xlsx

1) Commitment/cost: Are the "reserved" GPUs billed only for the POC period or do we need a minimum term? We prefer shorter commitment for trials.
2) Flexibility: Can we start with 1 x A100 reserved and rely more on burst capacity to keep initial cost lower, then bump to 2–3 if we see sustained load?

On traffic shape: our ops lead will send a one-page sample request trace (spikes every 10–15 minutes, heavy spikes at 11am/3pm PST). For now 1 x A100 reserved + autoscale to 6 sounds acceptable if we can confirm warm-up behavior and tail latency under spike tests.

Hi Marcus —

Quick note from CS: happy to own the POC acceptance run and keep the checklist moving. Based on Marcus' ask and Dev's workbook, I recommend the following small adjustments to reduce barrier to entry for the trial while giving us confidence in results: 

- Start: 1 x A100 reserved for Week 1 (onboarding + smoke tests), autoscale to max 6 x A100 for bursts.
- If during Week 2 we observe sustained >60% util for >3h, we’ll convert baseline to 3 x A100 for the remainder of the POC (mutual approval).

POC success gating (finalized):
1) Quality pass rate >= 85% on sampled human review (200 samples across test runs).
2) 95p latency <= 350ms for at least 3/5 load test runs covering peak patterns.
3) No more than 2 production-impacting incidents (errors causing >1% failed requests) across the 3-week test.

Milestones and owners: 
- Mar 9 (Kickoff): onboarding, whitelisting, runbook distribution — Owner: Dev (deliverables: runbook + whitelisting CIDRs).
